ledger.note: 350: Ran Min takes Ye and proclaims the Wei. 'In 350, Ran Wei usurped the throne of the Later Zhao dynasty in the city of Ye'; 'Ran Min proclaimed himself emperor of Wei amid the succession struggles of the Later Zhao dynasty' (Ran Wei-Later Zhao War page), after the prophecy 'After Zhao, comes Li'. The pages give the city, not a boundary.

Spring 351: Ran Min besieges Xiangguo. 'In the spring of 351, Ran Min besieged Shi Zhi's capital, Xiāngguó', where Shi Zhi had declared himself emperor; Shi Zhi asked Murong Jun of Former Yan for aid.

February 352: Xiangguo falls. 'By February 352, Ran Min had exterminated the Shi clan and conquered Xiangguo' (Conquest page); the Ran Wei-Later Zhao War page: 'The resulting war ended with a decisive victory for Ran Min.' The later-zhao dossier ends the Shi in 351.

February 352: Ran Min adds Xiangguo and the Shi remnant's land. 'Ran Min had exterminated the Shi clan and conquered Xiangguo from his general-turned-rebel, Liu Xian' (Liu Xian had killed Shi Zhi in 351 and held Xiangguo as the Zhao remnant); Xiangguo's population was moved to Ye. [Reviewer ea-03-x: holder named.]

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; slug ran-wei as the later-zhao (split 350, dissolve 351) and former-yan (gain 352) dossiers already use. Disagreement: the Ran Wei page and Conquest page have Xiangguo conquered by February 352 and Ye falling 8 September 352; former-yan's note says Ran Min was captured at Liantai and Ran Zhi captured 'ending Ran Wei' without a month. The later-zhao dossier dates the Shi end 351 (infobox) while the Conquest page puts the Shi clan's destruction by February 352 (the War page: spring 351 siege); I kept the later-zhao counterpart for the Xiangguo gain. The pages give no provinces for Ran Wei; Ran Min's claimed reach (You province, Changshan and Zhongshan commanderies) is intent or foraging only. Month 9 of the ledger events is the page's 8 September 352. The Wuxiang / Jie massacre of 350 is not in the ledger (no territory).
